title: The Eastern Shores of the Adriatic in 1863
subtitle: With a Visit to Montenegro
short_title: The Eastern Shores of the Adriatic
summary: In the summer of 1863 Emily, Viscountess Strangford, a daughter of the hydrographer Sir Francis Beaufort, travelled up the eastern side of the Adriatic. Starting from Corfu in June, she rode through southern Albania, by Delvino and Zitza, to Ioannina and the mountains of Suli; a chapter ends with notes for travellers on money, horses, seasons and game. She then went by Austrian steamer along the coast to Ragusa and the Bocche di Cattaro, and up to Tsetinje, where she was received by Prince Nicholas of Montenegro, Princess Milena and the Prince’s father, Mirko. In July she went on through Dalmatia, by Spalato and Salona, Sebenico and Zara, to Fiume and along the coast of Istria to Trieste, writing of churches, towns, dress and the people she met. Three chapters by her husband, Percy Smythe, Viscount Strangford, are political essays on Corfu, northern Albania and the Eastern Question.
